agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse. Multi-voice novel with two genuinely different narrating positions, not a diary. (a) Retrospective strands: third-person past narration of several named characters (Louise, Lena, Nel) plus a first-person voice speaking apostrophically to a dead addressee in past tense (q01607, q01609, q01626, q01636). (b) Simultaneous strands: third-person PRESENT scene narration (q01633 'she starts to beg... She wants to go back'), a first-person present voice (q01595, q01618, q01624), and present-tense setting/legend passages about the river and Beckford (q01608, q01610, q01622). The present minority is therefore structural -- an identifiable set of strands -- rather than noise or recollection. Expect SPLIT_REVIEW; the cause is 'mixed -- strand'. Watch q01608/q01610/q01622: they are present-tense story-world exposition rather than character scenes, and a reader who filed them as gnomic would push the book to 22 past / 5 present (81% past) and flip it to HIGH CONF PAST. That is the single largest lever on this book's label.
